She is saved. Because the next time she is born, it will be with this thought. That is the secret of it. It is for that reason they are kept like that.

Whether it is a man or a woman, any thief or rogue, this thought will come to them at the time of death. They will pray with their hands on their chest, thinking, 'I could not achieve this.' Thus, in the next birth, they will be born into hell, and then they will live by crying out in pain, working, and suffering. Amidst that, saying, 'Oh God, if I had obtained this, I could have offered it to God,' they will share a portion of everything they get with God. Thus, they will accumulate merit. Have they not been saved? This will reach *dharma*, and then *karma*. See—*karma* and *dharma* will come together. Even if the husband objects, she will somehow hide a little for God. That is how she will live. Their children will also learn by observing this. They will hide even more for God than she did. In this manner, their lineage will be saved. That is what was said earlier. That one should get an opportunity to cry out and die like that.

As we do each of these things in this manner, our lineage will grow immensely. Pray with great agony for this. That is our weapon. I have only this prayer to give you. Pray, envisioning that God should do everything for this. Here, you—men and women, young and old—are striving very sincerely and spending money according to your abilities. If a small child weaves, the first earning from it is brought and offered here. We know what weaving yields today. There is a realm of such profound affection within this. We must respect it. It is inevitable that this will manifest either in you or at least in your lineage.

Having prayed for such a lineage, we have also gained good knowledge today. This is the will of God, not ours. Doing this prayer here cannot actually be called a prayer. Because it should be done by starving, crying out, and enduring hardship. Here, you do not have to struggle like that. There are all kinds of facilities. God has provided you with that much comfort. God is thus making us do it with the power of command. You, who were able to play a part in it, will have positions and honors; that is certain. But it is enough if you do not develop the tendency, as mentioned earlier, to do half of this and then lose everything in the end. Even if you live for only four days, those four days should be lived virtuously. May you attain that course of *karma*! You must live understanding this.

From today onwards, we will lead a good life. Go forth praying with the determination that we shall strive for a better tomorrow. When you come next time, go forth praying with a little more resolve or a little more strength. Thus, become stronger each time. Ultimately, people will only be able to see you as role models. Conduct yourselves in such a way that others feel that what you say is right and that is the world. Do it, recognizing it as your need. That is what is required.
Guruvani
February 1985

Everything we do with penance and other rituals has a result. It has often been informed that this is not a lineage with the corresponding knowledge. In the experience up to this day, it feels exactly like that. The reason is that such spiritual knowledge does not exist among us. We do not largely accept the principles of psychic powers (*siddhi*) or other principles of *karma*. However, there is belief in *karma*. The wise can untie that *karma* through faith. That is why it is said that self-realized souls do not accept it. We will only see one or two such self-realized souls in our entire lifetime. We might sometimes see plenty of others. Although one may find a yogi, a performer of *karma*, and a devotee, the self-realized soul will be rare.

Those with some experience explain and inform us about the merits of this yoga, *karma*, and the like. However, self-realization begins only beyond Devendra. When speaking of the position of Devendra, it stands at the sixth state. So, it begins from the point where the Indra of the devas and the lord of the *ganas* stand. The stance of the wise is that whatever exists up to that point cannot be called self-realization. But here, we often proclaim those who practice devotion for ten or twenty years as great self-realized souls and knowledgeable beings. This is something that remains confined merely to the knowledge of past incarnations. Such knowledge refers to an assembly consisting of all demons, all deities, sages, ascetics, and the wise. That is why it was said that not many such knowledgeable self-realized souls appear among us. Not all of us can reach that level of knowledge either. Furthermore, it is only three hundred years after their time that people begin to praise and acknowledge their glories.

If such a great soul arrives, this is how we can understand their nature: they will always show us affection in a very profound manner. It will also be accompanied by a majesty that makes it impossible for us to ever forget them. Yet, within that, the disciplinary nature will not be absent. They might discipline us in every way. But we lack the knowledge to humbly listen to or understand all of that. The reason for that is the previously mentioned lack of acquaintance. Even if we fall into the ignorance of not being able to implement what we received in our time, we should at least have the wisdom to see, hear, and accept it. There is a tendency among us to reject and dismiss everything. There are many who assume that if they mock and dismiss everything with contempt, others will believe them to be very great.

It is not that kind of knowledge which is being discussed here. This is extremely profound. It has been thirty-three years since I had the experience. However, we happened to receive this in return through its aspect of wisdom only from 1973 onwards. Prior to that, the aspects of the Trimurti were underway. Numerous difficulties and hardships had to be endured for that. Its other aspects are still not concluded today. That is, a deity, a goddess, or even a minor deity is proclaimed with immense significance in our Vedas, Puranas, and even the Upanishads in the position of visibly manifest *dharma*. When Vedantins come here, they speak of all this as eclipsed matters. Similarly, when we had the experience, it seemed like a great wonder to those who were with me at the time. Then, it became very troubling for them—wondering whether all that had happened was false or not.

The words given by those under the Trimurti, and by the Trimurti themselves, later came to a state where we could not use them. We did not know what it was. It was a condition where we could not comprehend whether it was our fault or some other deficiency on our part. We ourselves did not know what everything that occurred prior to eleven years ago actually was. It was from the eleventh year onwards that each of these things began to be understood in this manner. By the fifth year, we were able to firmly establish the conviction that we would definitely make no mistakes hereafter. Yet, we have not been able to implement it among the people. Very few people have understood this even today. Even among the believers, those who have comprehended this fully would not amount to even two percent. It is a scenario of that nature. We are instructed to acquire this through our *karma*. It has been informed that a conviction should be established in all of you who come here, and by acting according to that conviction, through your progeny, proportional to the magnitude of our present deeds, they are to become great souls subsequently. This occurs for the third generation.

However, the children being born at present possess merely a fraction of knowledge. We know from our experience that the children born today are more intelligent than those of past eras. Yet, even they possess only a very limited extent of knowledge. A distinct birth is ordained for the third generation—they are none other than our ancestors (*Pitrus*). The ancestors, which means the great souls existing in various realms such as *Devas*, *Rishis*, *Yogis*, and *Sanyasis*, will relinquish this ancestral state. Upon relinquishing this state, in accordance with the divine resolve (*Brahmanishchaya*), they stand poised as the rightful claimants to incarnation. Now, among the current believers, the second generation will attain a state of absolute faith. It is to them that these ancestors, possessing the rightful claim to incarnation, are waiting to be born. Therefore, you who are householders (*Grihasthashramis*) must exercise immense caution. The immense magnitude of the deeds we perform today defies verbal articulation.

The purpose behind the incarnation of these children has been revealed. That purpose will commence here after a span of twenty years. After these years, a substantial transformation will occur even within our present system of governance; this will manifest through the children born after 1973. However, it is the children born twenty years later who will ascend to this position of knowledge. It is for this very reason that you were advised to exercise such profound caution.

Among the revelations received, millions of ancestors—*Rishis*, as well as those under the dominion of the *Trimurti* and *Manu*—came forward and declared that this must be attained through *Karma* (action). *Karma* signifies that even our slightest movement constitutes an action. This is precisely why it has been stated that these ancestors will incarnate only within those of the second generation who are capable of attaining absolute faith.
Guruvani
March 1985

You possess certain deficiencies. What are they? The *Karma* accumulated from the deeds of our ancestors is on one side. The second factor stems from the circumstances in which we are born and raised. Thus, both these elements have taken hold of us. They have manifested within the individual soul (*Jeeva*). However, when this soul begins to function, our inherent tendencies (*Vasanas*) merge with the *Karma* of our ancestors, rendering us unable to accomplish tasks to completion. This is the underlying cause. How much time is required for you merely to comprehend this concept? Consequently, you lack the inherent inclination to undertake a *Karma* of such vast magnitude. To provide a brief illustration: right here amongst us, there are those who exhibit the utmost devotion, as well as those who claim to believe but waver intermittently. None among them hesitates to assert that their own actions are unequivocally correct. We even have individuals among us who harbor the notion that if a task cannot be accomplished through them, its ultimate failure is of no consequence. Can this be considered appropriate? 'I am insignificant in this grand scheme; what remains is merely an entity called "I." I am oblivious even to the extent of what can be accomplished through it. Let me attempt an effort at least akin to that of an ant'—this tone of supplication is absent within you. Instead, there exists an egoistic sense of 'I.' Entangled within that ego, clinging to the accumulated conditioning (*Samskaras*) of myriad past lives, manifesting as a primal instinct clinging desperately to existence like a biting ant facing death, how can we possibly internalize and attain this? We harbor a pervasive arrogance that brazenly claims, 'My ancestors, my associates, or my contemporaries have accomplished everything and bequeathed it to me, and I am fully aware of it.' Therefore, it is practically impossible for us to undertake this collectively. Nevertheless, if we proceed with steadfast faith, we can achieve a certain degree of comprehension. 'O Divine, I lack the capacity to execute this. May my lineage, at the very least, be endowed with that capability'—you must cultivate this attitude of absolute surrender.

Revelations have been provided regarding the progression of this lineage. Thus, amidst the multitudes of *Rishis* and entities belonging to various other classifications, a select group of Brahmin ancestors—encompassing Brahmin *Rishis*, *Sanyasis*, and *Yogis*—was observed. The specific reason they were distinguished is that they represent a lineage that historically wielded Vedic authority within the *Varnashrama Dharma*. Naturally, the remainder consists of ancestors to whom such authority, erudition, or supreme wisdom had not been transmitted. It is for this reason that the former group was explicitly emphasized. On the very day this spiritual endeavor (*Karma*) was initiated here, they arrived and pleaded, 'You must salvage us.' The response they received was, 'So be it, but let it be for a later time.' However, upon their subsequent return, twenty-five percent of them were assimilated into the Absolute (*Brahman*). The remainder continue to wait. Their aspiration is to attain assimilation through the merit generated by the *Karma* we are poised to undertake. Those who remain number approximately two to three hundred thousand. You must comprehend the statistical magnitude: these two to three hundred thousand exist amidst hundreds of millions of individuals.

From the standpoint of true knowledge, one must ponder how a *Karma* of such immense magnitude has been entrusted to us—individuals who lack even the rudimentary awareness of the most diabolical and debased demonic entity. There is but a singular explanation we can offer for this. It is unequivocally nothing other than the divine resolve (*Brahmanishchaya*). There exists a profound rationale behind the divine resolve manifesting in this manner. One contributing factor is the cyclical progression of the four *Yugas* (epochs). The other pertains to the lineage of *Manu*. Subsequent to an undetermined disruption within *Manu's* lineage, the *Trimurtis* were instituted. However, the *Trimurtis* found themselves unable to advance further. The underlying cause for this stagnation culminates with *Devendra*. Consequently, there remains no inherent right to ultimate liberation (*Mukti*). Furthermore, *Devendra* himself languishes beneath the affliction of a mortal's curse. We must therefore comprehend that even *Devendra* occupies a state vulnerable to human malediction. This serves as compelling evidence of the exalted heights humanity can attain through righteous living. And this holds true even during this era of the *Shudra*. The term *Shudra* denotes one bereft of true knowledge. The epoch of the *Shudra* is the *Kali Yuga*. Operating under the delusion of possessing supreme wisdom, hastily intervening in all matters without a definitive resolve and acting devoid of righteous *Karma*—such is the nature of this era. It is precisely within such a tumultuous historical juncture that we have been incarnated. Yet, to ensure that this divine purpose manifests within humanity, the Supreme Being has been meticulously arranging the sequence of events since antiquity.

The epoch of the *Shudra* commences with the advent of Sri Krishna. Within our southern Indian region, particularly in Kerala, aside from the selective elevation of a few individuals from the *Shudra* strata, the broader populace has remained devoid of intellectual enlightenment. Furthermore, this elevation largely occurred under the auspices of brute force, categorizing them akin to brigands—pertaining to instances where political authority was usurped through mere physical might. A trajectory that initiated with the *Ettuveetil Pillamar* ultimately met its definitive conclusion during the reign of Chithira Thirunal. Yet, in this societal framework, the privilege of communal dining (*Panthibhojanam*) was strictly prohibited to all save the royal lineage. Such was the prevailing interpretation of *Vedic Dharma* in this region. What profound knowledge could possibly be derived from such practices? Are these selectively elevated *Shudras*, or indeed anyone else, cognizant of higher truths? Their existence is restricted to base consumptive acts, sartorial displays, superficial pageantry, musical recitations, and ritualistic processions (*Thalappoli*). Consequently, the collective intellect of our society—the knowledge inherent to the *Shudra* state—has descended to abysmally low levels. Correspondingly, scriptural exegesis was reduced to the mere recitation of mythological texts (*Puranas*), casually appended with a superficial gloss of *Advaita* philosophy. We are the very progeny of such profound ignorance. Ergo, it is improbable that individuals such as ourselves will attain immediate spiritual realization. Nevertheless, through an act of divine grace, you have been granted incarnation. This grace lies precisely in the fact that we have been incarnated during this very *Kali Yuga*. The *Kali Yuga* is fundamentally an era of hybridization and syncretism. The state itself is characterized by syncretism. Consequently, every consumable commodity is a hybrid. This constitutes the ultimate triumph of the *Bhagavad Gita* and its author. In contemporary times, whether among humanity, the avian and animal kingdoms, the botanical world, or even our sustenance, nothing remains free from hybridization. This hybridization extends even to parental lineages. To rationalize this, individuals construct the apologetic argument: 'If Panchali was permitted such liberties, why should we be denied?' This rationalization is applied to figures we traditionally venerate and revere. Yet, their comprehension is strictly limited to the numerical aspects of the narrative; they remain entirely oblivious to the profound esoteric significance of Panchali. We constitute a hybrid demographic, executing our *Karma* in a state of disarray and leading profoundly impure lives. Regardless of the counsel offered, an individual in this state may not spontaneously embrace a purified existence. Sage advice may entirely fail to penetrate their intellect. Alternatively, we are burdened by a pathological tendency to pursue perceived 'goodness' while simultaneously deriding and humiliating the very sources of wisdom. This paradigm must undergo a radical transformation. Even if no other grand objective is realized, this detrimental disposition must be eradicated from within us, allowing this very hybridization to serve as the catalyst for the purification of our existence. This process is entirely analogous to the horticultural technique whereby a grafted tree, capable of yielding exquisite fruit, is cultivated from the rootstock of an ordinary indigenous mango sapling.

This is a path bestowed by the divine will of Brahman to attain purity in this state. It is a path of action (Karma) that enables one to reach, through their own deeds, the realm inhabited by ancestors, deities, sages, ascetics, yogis, and the enlightened. We have been granted the authority to bestow birth, to impart the karma necessary to grant liberation to others and unify them with Brahman, and to perform actions for the pure karma of the children yet to be born into this lineage. This is its path. It currently remains in its primordial form. We have not progressed significantly forward. Henceforth, the authority over this rests with you.

The reason it was stated that a lineage is essential for those who believe in this tradition and pass through it is that your ancestral identity must be dissolved from there. How should it be dissolved? It must be dissolved through liberation. The karma to grant liberation to our chosen deities whom we have worshipped—whether they are referred to as Devas or Brahmarakshas—will eventually come into our hands. This is our appointed karma.
Guruvani
April 1985

You have been designated as the custodians of a karma that purifies in this state. However, we require the knowledge to solidify that understanding, to think expansively, and to acquire that karmic competence. That is our ultimate goal. Today, we are only capable of transmitting that knowledge to our successors. One should not assume that anything else can be done. If anything else is attained, it is solely the resolve of Brahman. It belongs neither to you nor to me. You must disseminate knowledge of this nature.

Who will be the progeny capable of grasping this knowledge? It is described as the incarnation of a Guru who has guided millions of people. Descendants fortunate enough to facilitate the birth of such a great soul must be born among us. It cannot be conclusively stated that many have already been born. What we require today is a purity of karma to enable such births. To achieve this, rather than working in isolation and harboring the egoistic notion that 'I am superior' through individual actions, you must internalize the truth that 'I am nothing; I am merely a participant in a collective karmic endeavor.' Only then can you anticipate salvation and prosperity.

This is our path to salvation. True attainment is possible only when actions are performed with the profound dedication that 'we are essentially nothing; nevertheless, let us contribute to the best of our abilities.'

There is another profound reason for depicting the aforementioned Brahmin ancestors in such a manner. For them to be emancipated from the dominion of this deity, their salvation must occur through the position of a Guru. A Guru, therefore, is neither a deity, nor a sage, nor an ascetic. An ascetic attains liberation and departs. A sage transitions into an authority over a particular domain. A wise individual appreciates all these paths. While they may all be considered gurus in a sense, they are not the true Guru described here. Which Guru, then? It is not merely one capable of granting liberation to another sage. That is the essence of its meaning, contrary to common interpretations. The reality is that this concept remains misunderstood by you. Grasping this knowledge can be intellectually demanding. However, acquiring this wisdom is our imperative need today. By imparting it to our descendants, they may eventually offer guidance to our land, our nation, and the world. This is not an avenue for acquiring immediate wealth, nor is it a forum for mundane inquiries such as diagnosing an illness. This is pure knowledge. The crucial question is our stance in relation to this knowledge. In this regard, we have been bestowed with the opportunity to fervently invoke the divine, even in our state of ignorance. Therefore, it is essential that you all invoke the divine collectively and with utmost sincerity.

What we witness in the world today is merely superficial. We are destined to ascend to a significantly higher state. That time will come; an intimation of this has already been received. We represent the primordial lineage of this transformation. According to the divine resolve of Brahman, the lineage of Manu and the lineage of the Trimurti are being unified to initiate the creation of an entirely new lineage. This is our role. It is a nascent sprout of that divine will. We have been entrusted with the foundational path to cultivate this sprout. Understanding this, you must achieve karmic purity devoid of any discriminatory intellect, derive wisdom from it, attain competence through that wisdom, and when fortune aligns, everything will manifest in its rightful place. We must remain vigilant until that opportune moment arrives. One must not succumb to arrogance upon acquiring partial knowledge, nor exhibit insolence upon accumulating material wealth. Such detrimental traits must be entirely eradicated from our character.

As previously articulated, the Shakta, Shaiva, and Vaishnava traditions of the Trimurti lineage converged into a singular entity, transitioning into the wisdom of Manu's lineage. That wisdom is now undergoing a transformation, paving the way for the knowledge that catalyzes a new creation, which is what is being discussed here. The foundational karma for this endeavor is what now rests upon us.

Presently, there may be both theists and atheists among you. Regardless of your stance, remain steadfast in your conviction. One must not oscillate between the two. Adopting faith merely when health and vitality decline is ultimately futile. You must firmly demonstrate your conviction while you possess health and vitality. The responsibility to substantiate the nature of disbelief also rests entirely upon you.

When I first arrived here, there was an elderly gentleman who would visit with a rusted sword tucked under his arm. He would approach me to discourse on Vedanta, often beginning with, 'I had an uncle named Pillai. My Pillai uncle is in a state of Samadhi.' This is not the type of knowledge we ought to propagate. Despite our insignificant stature, we have been presented with profound revelations, including the lineage of the prophets. Their legacy is by no means insignificant; in fact, it is somewhat more extensive than ours. This is because the domain encompassing the Hindu identity was once more vast. However, the reverberations of the virtuous karma associated with the Hindu identity were primarily confined to India or the regions historically integrated with it. There are numerous nations across the globe where Hindu Dharma is virtually non-existent. When evaluated from this global perspective, the reach of the Trimurti system is quite limited.
Guruvani
May 1985

Today, adherents of all religions and individuals from all strata of society have migrated into India. Yet, when evaluated collectively, we constitute a very minuscule fraction of the population. You remain oblivious to this reality. Unwittingly, you carry a narrative, instilled by others, that falsely amplifies your own greatness. This Earth is the dwelling place of countless nations. A comprehensive census of global populations remains elusive, rendering other demographic comparisons moot. It is insufficient to merely assert and convince ourselves of our own grandeur; one must also critically examine the realities illuminated by practical experience.

Therefore, in this context, we are akin to individuals attempting to lasso a mountain of grandeur with a mere cotton thread—not even a resilient one. Yet, with this fragile thread, we aim to conquer this mountain. This is because the prevailing current is favorable to us. Aligned with the trajectory of this current, we are merely proceeding while holding onto this thread, as if hauling a conquered mountain. We must interpret our situation with precisely this understanding, acknowledging our limited capabilities. However, present circumstances are advantageous to us. Advantageous to whom? To the uninformed masses scattered across the globe. The term 'Shudra' signifies the ignorant. Kali Yuga is the epoch of the Shudra. You possess tangible evidence of this within yourselves. The educational opportunities available here were not benevolently apportioned to us by the traditional Brahmin and Kshatriya elites. Rather, we gained access to them through the inevitable progression of time. This is what is meant by the current being favorable to us. We are immersed in this current; essentially, we are fortunate to have been born in this specific era.

Today, we are in a position where everything we touch yields fruit. The oppressive practices of untouchability, unapproachability, and social exclusion have been eradicated. Presently, there is universal freedom in these matters. Therein lies our triumph. We have now acquired the capacity to govern and to administer. What remains is the acquisition of the profound knowledge discussed earlier. Subsequently, through rigorous contemplation and the purity of our actions, we must integrate this wisdom as our own.

There are certain things that women in our homes must be very careful about. There is no mother in this world who does not think, in the name of some belief, that 'my daughter should get this,' 'my husband should get that,' or 'my children should have all these things.' Therefore, when you perform every action (karma), it should be with the thought that it must bring goodness to the world and to your progeny. Similarly, if it is a father, he should not think, "I am unable to perform karma even for the two children in this house." Instead, the thought should be, "May they have an existence in every way, to provide for ten people, to eat, and to wear." Whether one is a cart driver, a boatman, or anyone performing any task, if he is a father, he must possess this knowledge. One must not embody laziness. We can perform any karma; you should not assume that it is merely for feeding the family. It might be a small thing. However, the knowledge, experience, and tradition that your progeny acquires through your actions must stand as the foundation for the world and for this lineage. First, you must acquire that knowledge. Then, impart it to your descendants. This is our goal.

Therefore, all these ancestors (Pitrus) mentioned to us for this purpose, the previously mentioned Brahmin ancestors, the reason they are called so is because they are the progeny of those with knowledge. Due to that knowledge, they attained the position of a Deva. They are unable to descend from this Deva state. A Deva also does not have the authority to grant liberation (Mukti). This is because he does not possess karma. He has a subtle body (sookshma sareera). Then how can he achieve it? He cannot. That is why they appeal to be born into a lineage that possesses purity of karma (karma shuddhi).

Once their merits (punya) are exhausted, they fall back into the human world. Their desire is that this fall should be into this very lineage. Then, starting from scratch, they achieve completeness through karma and attain liberation through birth. Thus, whether you are male or female, you must make a firm resolution: "I, who am to be the master of karma of this standard, shall not tread the path of error anymore." You must muster this courage: "An opportunity to see, hear, and understand this has come to me; I shall reclaim it."

Without understanding this, tomorrow a sorcerer (mantravadi) or an astrologer might come, scratch his head, and say, "I see the influence of Gulikan in this." If asked for a solution, this ritualist will say, "No problem, just call a priest (Tirumeni) there, perform Tilahavanam, Shuddhihavanam, and Kshetrapindam, and grant purity to this ancestor." He does not know who this Gulikan is or how this Gulikan can be controlled. We perform these acts without knowing the position of this Gulikan, Deva, or Devi, or what the qualification of this karma is. This is where we fail. That is a science created during the time of the Devas to reveal the meaning of the Deva lineage.

However, if you examine the Siddha Panchangam, it prescribes that we can have such karma performed by a person akin to a sage (Jnani), it can be performed in any condition, and there is no Rahukalam for him. You must have it done with this understanding. This is said so that the magnitude of what is being done can be understood.
Guruvani
June 1985

You have been conducting Pournami prayers here for quite some time. You are doing it even more intensely than the temple traditions. However, you have a shortcoming. That shortcoming is incompatible with our present desire. That shortcoming did not occur by itself; it was brought about. This is due to our fundamental ignorance. I have said before that only ascetics (sanyasis) observed the Pournami vow (vrata). They did this because the course of karma would be completely severed. But you have not understood that. You only possess the knowledge that follows certain poets who have prescribed a specific result for each vow. You must understand three things. First, how should our belief be recorded? Second, is this belief meant to eliminate our course of karma, or is it to ward off some other sinful power? Third, are you doing it merely as an offering (nercha)?

Among us, the worship of God is unknown. We only know offerings (nercha). "I shall offer this to that place for this purpose"—such things are more prominently reflected among us. This was sufficient in the Treta and Dvapara Yugas. This is because, at that time, they had not attained the aspect called liberation for the soul (jivan mukti). No matter how high they rose, humans would only reach the position of a Deva. Therefore, it was not necessary then. It is not like that in Kali Yuga. We have assumed that nothing good will happen in the Kali age. However, we have been told that Kali is the most suitable time for everything. It is said that in Kali Yuga, the Shudra rules. 'Shudra' does not denote caste. Even within a single household, there are people of four castes: Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra. If we have ten members in our family, all four of these temperaments can be seen among them. Today, in our country, it has not been introduced in that manner. Our ancestors or statesmen introduced caste based on Varnashrama Dharma. Believing that there is no existence without caste, each of us is dealing with a situation where we live tied solely to that caste, enslaved by its specific karma or associated emotions. This must change from here. We who live in Kali Yuga must contemplate and understand the Dharma of Kali. The Dharma of Kali may sometimes be mentioned in the Puranas, Vedas, or Upanishads. Someone might have written it down. However, you will not be able to observe any of this. You simply cannot adopt the methods of the authors of these Puranas today. Furthermore, such a highly systemic (sastriya) life will not be practical for you today. While suffering from various such incapacities, you will not be able to complete these tasks. But we have an easier way.

Since the beginning of the world, that is, in this creation of Brahma (Brahmasrushti), a deluge (pralaya) occurs after the period of fourteen Manus. We do not even know what the duration is within that deluge. In the period called fourteen Manvantaras—the time of one Manu is seventy-one Chaturyugas. One Chaturyuga itself is twelve thousand divine years. A single divine year equals three hundred and sixty-five human years. In this, how much of a lifespan do we possess?

Although human lifespan is said to be one hundred and twenty years, is everyone able to reach that? Within this period, we must understand every kind of weight in the totality of our merits and sins. We do not even know what a life is. Our ancestors did not obtain that knowledge either. We have the habit and experience of living under the assumption that the Kali age is good for nothing. It is merely hearsay knowledge. We have no real information about it. In truth, that is not the case. Kali is the most suitable time for us to seek merit (punya). It is also the most beneficial time for women. Poets and others speak about women. Each of you should introspect and see how much truth you can speak in your life. In today's life, there are hardly any who speak the truth. The reason for this is the disorder that has crept into you due to habit. This habit exists because ignorant mothers raising children has continued as a lineage. They have only one thought: one child must be married off, and another must be brought in through marriage. They are raising children in such a state of frenzy. They want to show, "This is who I am." They are satisfied if they have ten children and the respective affairs are taken care of. Other than that, the capacity to think about what merit they need, why they did all this, or what must be done to prevent this wretched behavior of theirs from repeating in their children, is completely absent in their lives. Therefore, even if such knowledge is spoken of, you will not understand it.

I have already told you that there is an easy way for you now. We have been informed that once the world is created, a nature that subverts the will of Brahma could also occur in the world. To explain how that happens, after great Acharyas (teachers) were born and made their lives blessed, their successors came and, like watching a dance without knowing the story, did many things, as a result of which that history had to be rewritten. That is the reality. If a couple of hundred years pass like this, we will drift away from history in a way that we cannot even imagine.

The information is that twenty-five *Chaturyugas* have passed since such a thing happened in the world. A scenario where Brahma desired to bring about a change has been bestowed upon us in accordance with that divine will (*Brahma-nishchayam*). What this means is that, just as we do everything possible to raise our little children, for us who know nothing and lack scientific awareness or anything else, it is as if the will of Brahma has waited and provided this for us. While we receive it, you must understand this subject thoroughly. But you are not understanding this. There are many young people right here. Although they reside here, a conscious action corresponding to this does not arise in them. That does not mean you are committing a mistake. Because you lack the knowledge, you are unable to consciously grasp it and bring it into practice. It is the same with those who come and go here. This is the easiest era for you to change from this inherent nature. A path has been created here for you to receive knowledge from Brahma for this transformation.

This path is not one that has existed before. Through this path, we are growing as a *Guruparampara* (lineage of gurus). This is a great fortune for us. When we got the opportunity to be told this, every Acharya came and said, "Children; you must not go wrong!" This is the greatest thing we can attain in this world. It has been said that if you do not preserve this properly, after two generations have been careful, the third generation will destroy it, if you do not guide it straight.

This is not *Sannyasa* (asceticism). It is not a knowledge that we discovered and brought forth. We did not set out on our own to resolve some other mistake. Unknowingly, we, who were incapable, somehow fell into this light. After falling, when we lay there and flailed our arms and legs, each of these things was taught to us. You more or less know what is meant by flailing arms and legs. The times when I suffered hardships. What all insults I heard; I heard unbearable abuses. Most people know all this. They also know that none of the allegations heard were true. Today, that has become clear. So, it is not just about hearing abuses; the hardship endured for seventeen years is not small. It is the tenth year since understanding this. This has been received in the name of a great fortune. Even after being born and dying for aeons, there is no liberation for this except that husband, wife, children, and wealth will keep turning like a cartwheel. Because life revolves like this along with the world. But today it is not like that; since it is a *Guruparampara* that lays the foundation for that will of Brahma, we can achieve this.

You—as the ones who are to perform the primal duty (*Adikarma*)—Brahma Himself has brought you here. Like a blooming garden in a desert, this fortune has been given to you who possess no knowledge. This is only something that you can actively practice and achieve. You do not have to observe numerous fasts (*vratas*) or rituals for this. Sunday fast, Monday fast, Pradosha fast, Ekadashi fast—after observing numerous such fasts across countless lifetimes, the fast one must finally undertake is the Pournami fast. It is easy for you. With the Pournami fast, all other fasts can be avoided. The Pournami fast is the vow that makes one eligible for liberation (*Mukti*). You have been blessed with the fortune to observe the ultimate fast right at the beginning. It is the will of Brahma indeed that provided an opportunity for this.
Guru Vani
Birthday Message
August 1985

In Kerala, a special importance is given to the month of Chingam. Similarly, to the first day of the month of Medam. That can be seen all over India. If you look at the topography of Kerala, it is springtime itself. According to astrology, those born in the month of Chingam also deserve importance. Without relying on any other scientific rule, we celebrate Onam on an auspicious day in the month of Chingam. Referring to it as the 'Golden Chingam' (*Ponnin Chingam*), more importance is given to the month of Chingam than to all other months. It is the month sanctified by the birth of great souls for the awakening and upliftment of the *Avarna* (lower-caste) community. The time when the suppressed Asura emperor 'Maveli' steps out to visit his land. A month when Keralites do not hesitate to celebrate Onam for twenty-eight days. The time when the whole world jumps with joy and celebrates, waiting for the arrival of that great emperor who conducted a rule where hardship and sorrow never occurred. The month in which great souls take birth, imparting philosophical teachings to people who were subjected to untouchability through 'distance and touch' (*theendal and thodeel*), enabling them to attain prosperity and progress by forgetting caste and religious differences. In every way, an auspicious time. On this occasion, may we attain the knowledge and wisdom to view, in accordance with the times, the great souls who gave us the opportunity to think about what our land, our people, and the world need.

The time today is Kali (Kali Yuga). History and science help us understand that the Satya, Treta, and Dvapara yugas had their own unique conditions. Then we must know that Kali also has a designated state. The announcement of the ancestors is also the same. Nature is proclaiming to us that it is absolutely true. From the time of Lord Krishna, the land of Bharath has witnessed the birth of numerous great souls who imparted noble knowledge, sacrifice, and purity of action to the Shudra class as a whole and to the believing public in particular. But all this has been disrupted by the Avarna-Savarna distinction and the *Varnashrama Dharma*. The temple system, which brought Vedic dharma through rituals, incorporating worship like the Shaktheya tradition, its associated mantras, tantras, festivals, and various arts extending up to the Devadasi system, navigated us on a path that introduced us to the abyss from the heights. From this, caste was created, and from caste, sub-castes were created. An administrative system that properly enforced untouchability by prescribing distance and touch onto the illiterate poor, along with the kings required for it, existed all over Bharath. Through this, the Avarna system persisted. They lived a life with no duty towards themselves, their home, or their country. That life, over time, completed the system of slavery. That is why our country came to be ruled and made to be ruled by another group.

Although it fostered education, wealth, and enlightenment, the excessive infatuation towards Western lands by administrators who tried to bring about changes over time did not consider that it would weaken the people to the point of stifling the voice of life crying out in distress, becoming debilitated like a patient afflicted by inescapable karmic faults in life. This is a time highly suitable for the resolution of karma (*karma-nivaranam*) by coming together in accordance with the guidance of great souls to view this with value, with the determination and vigor that the goal of life is to impart peace and tranquility, providing a time for not just the Avarnas but also the Savarnas to correct their mistakes and move forward, and to show a 'better tomorrow' where there is no Avarna-Savarna divide by including the Savarnas alongside the Avarnas. For example, it has shown us Ambedkar, who rose up in creation itself through his karma to write the Constitution from a position where the administrative sphere could not even be peeked into under any circumstance. Similarly, being born in this era, where our politics—advancing with socialism and other ideological codes without anyone realizing it—was blended with spirituality and portrayed like a historical truth to gain an administrative experience that does not consider gender differences, is a great fulfillment indeed. Praying to the Lord of the Universe (Jagatprabhu) that everyone may utilize their logic and intellect for actions that pave the way for the liberation of the soul, for the fulfillment of their material and spiritual life,
Your Swami
Guru Vani
September 1985

Because an error occurred in the previous lineage, it has not been possible to rectify it even after all this time. Today, each of us frequently says this. Similarly, Vedantins and scholars often use the phrase '*Aham Brahmasmi*'—meaning, 'I am Brahman'. However, it is worthwhile to consider whether we are truly entitled to say this about ourselves. Upon logical reflection, it is evident that it is untenable. What authority do we have to proclaim that we are Brahman? This is a fundamental flaw that crept into Hindu Vedanta. There is a widespread tendency among us to invoke Vedanta for everything. If you visit southern Travancore, even the pan-shop vendors will speak of Vedanta. This is not the case in the north. People have no hesitation in making casual remarks like, "That is how it should be, and it will happen." They say this not out of profound knowledge, but from mere hearsay. Repeating this incessantly, we eventually arrived at the phrase '*Aham Brahmasmi*'. None of us possesses the authority to declare this. We respect our father, but we do not show respect by addressing him by his name. Nor do we claim that we are our father ourselves. Our primary shortcoming is that we have not accorded even that basic level of reverence to this concept. Our Vedantins have taught us to address God as "You". That is permissible. This practice is most prevalently used in the Islamic faith. Prayers are offered by addressing the divine as "You". In recent times, it was Sree Narayana Guru who addressed the divine as "You". He stated, "You are Truth, Knowledge, and Bliss." Thus, one can pray by addressing God as "You". At the same time, it must be a prayer infused with a profound sense of dedication when using "You". Otherwise, it is inappropriate for individuals of a lower spiritual standing to do so. Is it not a misfortune if we fail to cultivate a capacity for true reverence? When the eloquence of prayer is replaced by mere logic, even if it is technically correct, does it not lose its profound humility? However, when a sense of absolute dedication arises, we can certainly practice it. There is nothing wrong in doing so.

Here, even that has not been accomplished. We are actively being corrected. First, it was explicitly stated that we cannot use this term 'Brahman' so casually. Besides this, a statement was also provided to correct how we should properly perceive the concept of Brahman. We have long suffered from an inherent inability to foster true reverence. This deficiency has existed since the era of the *Trimurti*. We mold a piece of cow dung to represent Lord Ganesha. We place a flower on top of it. After a short while, we simply discard it. When women in the south perform the *Pongala* ritual, they consecrate Ganesha in such a remarkably trivial manner. This is not practiced in the north. In the north, they perform a ritual called *Udaya Pooja* once a year. Furthermore, it is not conducted in individual households. An entire agricultural field in a specific region is prepared for this purpose, and the people of that area gather to perform it collectively. It is executed with the utmost purity. These are practices established by our ancestors. The knowledge we have inherited suggests that none of this is entirely correct. Along with '*Aham Brahmasmi*', there also emerged the notion that the Shudra class is strictly forbidden from acquiring the knowledge of Brahman (*Brahmajnana*). Consequently, we find ourselves in this current predicament today. The mythological story of Vamana illustrates how a monarch who meticulously upheld truth and righteousness was trampled down into the netherworld simply because he was not a Brahmin. If a deity can trample down an emperor in such a manner, what prevents them from trampling us? Was it not a deity who descended and stomped on him? This fate befell Mahabali solely because he lacked the label of a Brahmin. His only crime was that someone who was supposedly prohibited from practicing truth and righteousness actually successfully upheld them. This reveals the deeply degraded and prejudiced history preserved by our ancestors. The writers of that era were merely mercenaries who penned such narratives for financial gain.

In a similar vein, we have managed to persistently worship the exact opposite of whatever constituted the truth. Suchindram serves as a prime example. That is the very place where the *Trimurti* were utterly defeated and humiliated. Yet, today, it is the *Trimurti* who are worshipped there. What exactly does this defeat entail? The myth states that when the wife of a sage sprinkled the holy water used to wash her husband's feet, the *Trimurti* were instantly transformed into mere infants. This narrative is formally inscribed and illustrated there. It is also claimed that Devendra attained purification (*shuchi*) from that sage. That is precisely how the name Suchindram originated. Subsequently, Devendra is worshipped there. Whose fabrication is this? Are you not familiar with that story? When the *Trimurti* were turned into infants, their respective wives purportedly came to beg for their marital bliss and, by sprinkling holy water once again, restored them to their original forms. However, because the infants looked identical, they had to undertake severe penance just to identify their own husbands. Devendra, upon learning of this, came to the exact spot where Sage Atri had meditated, performed penance himself, and attained purity. Whose lie is it to continue worshipping Devendra there? They invent elaborate stories for this exact purpose. Vishnu worships Shiva. Shiva worships Vishnu. Both of them together worship Shakti. Besides these convoluted and repetitive tales, have these Vedantins or the worshippers of the *Trimurti* ever managed to articulate anything with absolute conceptual clarity? Every single one of us must critically ask this question. Since that time, Brahman has been attempting to reform them. The *Trimurti* did not manifest on their own. They were created specifically to rectify the fundamental errors of Manu. The *Devas* are inherently hedonistic. There is not a single narrative about a *Deva* that does not involve romantic or sexual exploits. The *Deva* is far more worldly than an ordinary human being. Thus, does a *Deva* even possess the time or inclination to attain liberation (*mukti*) or achieve purity of action (*karmashuddhi*)? There is merely a momentary blessing. Then, an immediate curse. That is all there is to it. For a long time, neither has been effectively occurring. We have unfortunately fallen for this mythological narrative. We must be capable of fundamentally altering this perspective. It is in this precise context that we have received the sacred word from Brahman.

There have been individuals in the past who successfully transcended the state of the *Trimurti*. Consider the *Parayi Petta Panthirukulam* (the twelve children born to a Pariah woman)—there is only one female among them. That is Avvaiyar. All twelve of these individuals surpassed the elevated status of the *Trimurti*. They conclusively demonstrated that they could achieve far more in this earthly realm than the *Trimurti* themselves. Poets have traditionally elevated the *Trimurti* and enshrined them at the absolute pinnacle. However, the children of the Pariah woman treated this concept almost as a jest. For instance, the Vedic priests of Ambalappuzha failed miserably in their attempt to consecrate the goddess. The idol simply would not firmly set. It was only when Pakkanar entered, spat the remnants of his chewed betel leaves (creating a *thambalam* or spittoon), and performed the consecration that it firmly took hold. That is exactly how Thambalappuzha eventually became Ambalappuzha. A remarkably similar incident occurred at the Cherthala Karthyayani temple. Naranath Bhranthan caught a prawn, tied it securely with a string, dangled it, and was wandering along the road babbling like a madman. The Vedic priests had been desperately trying for three days, but the consecration would not fix firmly. He arrived, hung that very prawn right in front of the temple, went inside, and commanded the deity, "Sit here, woman," firmly establishing her presence. He even uttered two expletives. The consecration was perfectly secured.

No *Deva* holds any significance before a true *Jnani* (an enlightened sage). An individual named Gunangudi Masthan has also performed similar feats. Just like Naranath Bhranthan, the other eleven also logically and comprehensively rejected the conventional worship of *Devas*. They did not claim that God does not exist. Rather, they profoundly corrected us on who we should become and how we should conduct ourselves. Unfortunately, we were utterly unable to follow that enlightened path. That is the absolute truth. The exact same realization occurred in my own personal experience. When it powerfully manifested in my experience, a necessary correction was consequently received.

If you observe this vow (*vratam*) with strict discipline, you will attain a certain merit after completing fifty vows. Let us resolve to perform this properly for five years. If done for ninety days in the manner of an ascetic (*sanyasi*) within these five years, the result of five years will be achieved. Afterwards, it should not be done in that exact manner. Do it by changing the pattern. The Monday vows and Sunday vows of the past are no longer necessary. God has provided an opportunity to do only this for everything. What does this mean? In order to correct the mistakes made by our predecessors, we, who know nothing, have been brought to the forefront and made to undertake that karma. It is not the wise or the learned who are coming forward. It is for you and your children at the grassroots level to create the fruits of your karma as your own. Understand that this karma is what improves you. Since the time of Lord Krishna, karma has held a significant place. No god or goddess can bestow anything through blessings other than the merit of the karma performed by a human being. We used to believe they would. However, we have not been able to see it so far. You have received an opportunity for this. That is it. We celebrate the Pournami Vratam (full moon vow) here. But you must change your perspective a little. It is a vow for liberation (*mukti*) that supersedes all other vows. Yet, it is completely worldly as well. Why is it said that it grants the right to liberation and the right to complete worldliness? Both the sun and the moon have a role in the creation of all living beings. The sun brings about evolution in everything, just like a hen incubating its eggs. At the same time, the cosmic dust falling from the moon also has its own significance. The earth also has a role.

It is said that the growth and decline of this earth stem from our karma. India (Bharatam) is considered a good land. The Puranas state that being born in Bharatam is itself a great glory. The righteousness of Bharata's rule still exists here. Even though we have had the privilege of obtaining the best country on earth, blessed by the lives of the people of those times, the shortcoming that remains with us is our inability to imbibe its goodness. This must be changed. The divine will (*Brahmanischayam*) itself has brought us to the forefront to change this. To correct this aforementioned mistake, great souls were created initially. They were born here and there, imparted their teachings, and departed. Our ancestors, comprising Vedic scholars, pundits, and poets, have concocted several lame stories for us. Hearing those stories, we stand bewildered—wondering what to do next. You must understand this, act upon it, and come forward.
Guruvaani
October 1985

We are speaking by evaluating the fortune that shines through sacrifice, in light of the joys and sorrows experienced from the mistakes that have occurred in this world to date. How can we implement this? What is being implemented today? Having recognized the difficulties, virtues, and vices we have encountered so far, we must contemplate whether we can change our current habits, or if not, how we can rectify those mistakes if possible. Can we achieve this within the light of time? Many people have tried this in the past. It is not that everything failed completely; some things were successful. But today, we have taken up the complete form of the anomalies that emerged from it. That is to say, these are the individual subjects that have come down through numerous sages (*rishis*), wise men, ascetics, diligent householders, and lifelong celibates (*brahmacharis*). These are matters achieved by the actions of just two or four individuals among crores of people living. That itself will reach everywhere during their lifetime. Even in the present situation, religious scholars, Vedic experts, and scientifically minded individuals live in various parts of India. However, not everyone can internalize and act upon it. Some might be able to. One or two people might succeed through their actions. Even if it reaches us, to what extent can we reflect it? How much can we comprehend? Even if comprehended, how much can be implemented? How much can we ourselves carry forward to completion?

Looking at each of these, we might find that we haven't even been able to acquire knowledge equivalent to a handful of soil taken from a mountain. We cannot summarize such a vast subject. However, we must eliminate the present calamities by making small changes to the mistakes that have occurred over time. How? Everything evolves from the life involving father, mother, children, husband, and wife. Everything is gained from that. You should not even dream that ascetics or solitary Vedic scholars will accomplish this for you. Suppose someone from among you becomes an ascetic, a Vedic scholar, a wise man, or a karma yogi in isolation. Suppose he grows to his full potential through his sacrifice. How can this reach you, who grow without an element of virtue, a spirit of sacrifice, or class consciousness? How can you, being like that, carry this forward? You are ready to overthrow everything with the attitude that you are everything. Are you not living to pass on the origin of a lineage that fosters bad customs, destroys humility, and loses merit? Then can you reach anywhere? It is enough if you bear the responsibility of your home, land, and country. If you perform karma divided by caste or religion, you will only end up fighting each other and sowing the seeds of destruction. That will grow into a tree, bloom, and bear unwanted fruits, spreading further. Consider how much you can strive to prevent that ignorance from reaching you. You must live thinking of the single class called humanity, without caste, religion, or sectarian consciousness. You should be able to do at least that much. You are being given an opportunity to ensure that your life does not cause destruction to your neighbor or neighboring country. Our backward journey has been a review of how you can utilize this opportunity. We reflected on the extent to which the people of the past imparted good and evil; this is an opportunity to ponder whether we, who evolved from behind them, are at the forefront or the rear today. If you lose this opportunity, you will be able to do nothing.

When we think about this earth, which has existed for billions of years, our lifespan is so trivial. How can we act within this time to be useful for this lineage? Why did one come here? What can one do now to accomplish even an atom's worth of work for this world? Without thinking along these lines, it is said that there is anarchy all over the land. Anarchy of what? The discovery is that it is the anarchy of non-existence. What are we doing with what we have? Whether it is related to knowledge, statecraft, or our family life—how much are you utilizing it? Carrying a habit of incapability for anything as your asset, brimming with the attitude that "I am everything," aren't you living in every home acting as the patriarchal head of everything? Without self-cultivating dignity, and without removing these monetary or class-based perversions from among yourselves, how can you preserve your offspring as a lineage? You need to have foresight for this—that is, the householders. It will not suffice if ascetics or Vedic scholars foresee it. Each of your hearts is a center of knowledge that needs to be reclaimed by imparting your purity of character and simplicity to the people. You are draining it away, stuffing it with all sorts of unwanted things, and trying to reap its seeds. Men and women must resolve how to live from now on, understanding that such impurity has been imparted into us that we cannot even realize it is huddled inside the heart.

We do not conduct classes to impart evil; they are meant only to teach the good. However, what everyone tends to learn first is the bad. Recognizing this, even if our capacity to act is minimal, we must execute it with absolute purity. Every one of you possesses intellect. There may be some who are less intellectually endowed, yet everyone holds their own inherent potential. If we can channel that in a positive direction, each of us will become virtuous, and we will be capable of working to our fullest potential. Without this realization, all our endeavors will be in vain. Here, Vedanta is taught, Vedic rituals are taught, and statesmanship is taught. Yet, in all of these, one can observe the personification of selfishness. What is the use of establishing all this if you lack the sensibility of love? This cannot be achieved through your mischief or emotional outbursts. Nor can it be acquired merely by reveling in the tales of our ancestors. We are well aware of our ancestral history. According to Hindu conventions, there are four *varnas*. Among them, the Brahmin, Vaishya, and Kshatriya enjoy absolute freedom. Knowledge, administration, and Vedic rituals are their monopolies. The Shudra, who constitutes the lowest stratum, is forbidden from learning the alphabet. The scriptures dictated that if he were to learn, molten lead should be poured into his ears. Consequently, we are a lineage that has inherited only aberrations, devoid of any real knowledge. Our ancestors exhibited arrogance and a display of power, operating under the delusion of omniscience. Why did they become this way? They are the ones who were once subjected to beatings, lacking even the basic freedom to dress properly. If they went to the homes of the upper castes for food, they had to survive by gulping down water poured from a distance. They were the ones who starved, toiling until dusk for a mere measure of paddy. How could they survive on such a meager amount of paddy? How could they clothe themselves? How could they educate their children? The arrogance seen today is the flip side of that profound suffering. In contrast to the immense hardships endured by our ancestors, we face no such struggles today. It must be surmised that the very consciousness of freedom was entirely lost in those times. It was precisely when we were reduced to such a state of nothingness that adherents of other religions gained the liberty to enter this land. This can only be regarded as an act of divine providence.

Due to a historical inadequacy in the capacity to act in accordance with Dharma across different epochs, the Hindu systems of worship—Shaivism, Shaktism, and Vaishnavism—were subsumed. Instead of instilling the realization that an Advaitic essence encompasses all these traditions, the masses were led to their downfall through the mere preaching of Vedanta without true comprehension. Our lineage inherited the notion that scholars and sages were exceedingly formidable figures. This lineage merely sat in anticipation, much like a hornbill gazing at the sky for rain, devoid of any genuine knowledge. They existed without understanding the fundamental ways of life, the nature of a nation, or the mechanisms of governance. They remained ignorant of the necessities of individual households. Having originated in this profound ignorance, we must now, at the very least, propel ourselves toward true knowledge. Conversely, if we merely presume ourselves to be the repository of all knowledge, we shall remain stagnant. Therefore, as parents, you must lead an exemplary life. For this, faith must be anchored somewhere. To sustain this faith, we have embraced various mediums. Faith must evolve into a state where it is deeply loved, revered, and actively practiced. It is necessary to personify this faith, conceptualize it through various imageries, focus the mind upon it, and progressively impart wisdom from that focal point. This is the methodology adopted by Vedic practitioners and religious scholars. However, we are unaware of the depth to which this has penetrated. We have been existing in this condition for millions of years. Contemplate how such a faith can be transmitted and sustained. If we fail to impart this today, the consequences upon nature itself remain unfathomable. Nature encompasses all forms of destruction and sustenance. Primarily, one must reflect upon our fundamental sense of duty to preserve this nature, and subsequently act upon it. Failure to do so will lead you astray, precisely as it befell our ancestors. We must resolutely determine that such a fate shall not befall us again. Act with conviction, and everything will naturally align.
Guruvani
November 1985

The fundamental understanding of an 'Ashram' first emerged during an era when society lacked comprehensive awareness. (Today represents an age where everyone invokes the divine.) Ancient humans possessed greater longevity. Through relentless contemplation, even their vital force would generate immense spiritual heat. Righteous thought and conduct facilitate a balanced, moderate life. Society presumed that individuals leading such lives served as profound exemplars. That particular epoch possessed its own distinct characteristics. Subsequently, times changed. Today, Ashrams have proliferated even in rural villages. In the primitive stages, Ashrams were situated on secluded mountains. Why are Ashrams so ubiquitous in contemporary times? It is an inherent characteristic of the current era. The global population has expanded exponentially. In the past, human actions (*karma*) were driven by deep-rooted latent tendencies (*vasanas*). During those times, the population was sparse, space was abundant, and the intensity of *karma* was relatively subdued. The criteria for eligibility that exist today were absent then. In the modern context, qualifications, *karma*, and ultimate liberation (*mukti*) are often claimed merely by virtue of birth. What can be deduced from this? Even an individual who has merely functioned as a ritualistic practitioner (*karmi*) or lived as a *yogi* possesses this underlying *vasana* (for acquiring true knowledge). However, the manifestation of these tendencies varies significantly among individuals.

We tend to label all such inclinations as devotion (*bhakti*). Minor variations introduced over time gradually evolve into substantial disparities. Profound and rigid distinctions also emerge. By profound distinctions, I refer to the culmination of individual *karma*. In this context, there exist souls that have brought their respective *karmas* to fruition. Conversely, there are souls that have achieved completion in nothing. There are souls that have merely initiated the process. Some have progressed halfway, while others have completed three-quarters of their spiritual journey. Still, others have made only marginal progress. Every one of us operates across these myriad stages of spiritual evolution. Consequently, the latent tendencies (*vasana*) are never uniform across individuals; they vary significantly across the domains of *karma*, *bhakti*, and *jnana* (knowledge). Therefore, for those residing in an ashram, the experience is never monolithic—different individuals acquire distinct forms of knowledge. Even when a collective experience occurs, it is perceived in a thousand different ways by a thousand different people. This principle applies equally to *bhakti*, *karma*, and *yoga*. Minute discrepancies often go unnoticed. Both you and I may perform an action with devotion, yet the magnitude of that devotion varies. Such subtleties can only be discerned through prolonged temporal experience. Consequently, the true essence of ashram life is comprehended solely through sustained duration. Therefore, this understanding must be actively articulated and cultivated amongst us. We have lacked the tradition of such experiential instruction. It is for this reason that devotion continues to stagnate at its primitive stages—akin to the devotion prevalent during the *Treta Yuga*.

The paradigm of devotion characteristic of the *Treta Yuga* is insufficient to attain any elevated spiritual state in the contemporary era. The rationale is that in antiquity, realizing a spiritual experience required extensive epochs. That is no longer the case. Your individual soul (*jiva*) is an entity that has accumulated immense antiquity through a prolonged cycle of births and deaths. This evolutionary attainment manifests in multiple trajectories. One trajectory involves a soul that has acquired—or earned the karmic fortune of—action (*karma*) through devotion, merit (*punya*) through *karma*, and ultimate knowledge (*jnana*) through that merit. Another entity remains anchored in the desire for *karma*, while another yearns exclusively for knowledge. Furthermore, there are souls that have not yet even approached the realm of conscious *karma*; they have never harbored such aspirations.** These are souls that developed an inclination only upon witnessing these phenomena. How, then, can their spiritual progression reach completion? An innumerable multitude exists in precisely such disparate states in the modern era. It is inaccurate to postulate that devotion has diminished in contemporary times. Rather, amidst an intensification of this devotion, each of us is governed by distinct latent tendencies (*vasanas*). The fundamental cause of this divergence is the soul undergoing numerous incarnations, engaging in diverse *karmas* across expansive temporal spans. This includes circumstances of shared collective existence, followed by incarnations scattered across various geographical terrains, nations, and cosmic realms. Philosophical traditions postulate the existence of multiple such realms. Entities incarnated across such vast spectrums eventually converge at a singular spatio-temporal juncture.

There are quite a few people here living as householders. Even your own family members do not like you, do they? What is the reason for that? This phenomenon exists even among children born to the same mother. Shouldn't there be at least some affection in accordance with human values? Whether born to my mother, or an uncle's children, or a father's children, whoever they may be—didn't they grow up together? Shouldn't there be at least an understanding to respect the place where one has gone and not find fault with it? Shouldn't one go there and cooperate? Why doesn't that happen? It has been like this for many births. If someone comes here just to see you, they will say they are not entering inside. This essentially means they do not respect it. Why does that happen? They were born somehow. In those days, he might have been a servant. If he develops an affection for the house, then it is like the children of the same father. They are born like this. He will not get close. Whether male or female. There are some girls. They leave the house in a manner where they never get along with the family. Then they will never return to that house. That is the result of being ruined while working as servants in that house back then. They were born out of desire. After being born, they leave just like that. There are numerous such matters involved in this.

Just because you reside in an ashram, you will not automatically develop prudent care. Without that care, living in an ashram yields no result. So many people have lived alongside Sree Narayana Guru. They understood nothing. There was a time when Narayana Guru lay ill in a choultry. It was only three days prior to his Samadhi. He was crying out in pain, 'Ayyo, ayyo'. Many people assume that Narayana Guru should not experience such pain, or that Chattampi Swami should not experience this. They believe one should die with their head bursting—that is Samadhi. That is how many people perceive it. It is not possible to just burst and leave like that.

This is the Kali Yuga. How do people behave in the Kali Yuga? Gurus will arrive to guide them back onto a proper path. They differ from those who focus solely on their own lives, ascending like a beetle climbing a thread. You do not comprehend this karma. Those who ascend like a beetle on a thread do so solely for the sake of their own lives. There are those who absorb the flaws and burdens of numerous lives. Such a Guru cannot merely sit in one place and practice yoga. He may appear like a servant, or sometimes like a manager. Why is that? Only by acting in this manner can he nourish those standing nearby. Only if he behaves like a servant will such people approach him. Otherwise, they will not come. Sometimes like a scholar, sometimes like a sage, they can be seen manifesting four different characteristics simultaneously. To some, he appears as none of these, but rather like a great farmer. All these traits will manifest in them.

There is a section that describes the Avadhuta. It is not like this. He will behave like a ghost, like a madman. Going among people, he will behave without any distinction between men and women. That can occur even within an ashram. Does someone wandering like a madman possess any discipline? What does it matter to him whether he is in an ashram or at a public feast? To everything, he reacts as if he is mad. It is said they are like the wind and like growing children. Does anyone know which way the wind blows? Growing children will behave in various unpredictable ways. An Atmayogi is described as one who wanders devoid of illusions, devoid of ordinary intellect, and devoid of magic. None of these human illusions will be found in him. There will be no conventional logic. Devoid of intellect and magic—intellect implies a measured mind, a behavior that brings satisfaction to everyone; he does not possess that either. Then there is the complete trickster, the one who demonstrates magic. He doesn't have that either. Then how can one understand him? He might be seen at a public gathering or on the road. How can he be evaluated? Ordinary people cannot evaluate him. He is someone who has ascended solely through a state of yoga.

I will narrate an incident that took place in Neyyattinkara. There was a person named Keshava Sanyasi. He would gather rubbish and garbage lying on the road and tie it into a large bundle. He would place it somewhere and lie down. He would chew betel leaves and walk around with the juice drooling. Some people would come and buy tea for him. It would be tea purchased in the morning, with flies fallen into it. He would remove them and drink it. He would utter various things. Those standing around would realize that he was speaking about them. They were incoherent conversations lacking logical connection. He spoke about the specific matters of each individual standing in the crowd. They would understand it.

Once in Neyyattinkara, a woman in a house suffered from severe stomach pain. She couldn't even be transported to the hospital. He used to visit the neighboring house. The husband of the woman, who was writhing in agony, ran to him and informed him. He went to that house, removed the woman's clothes, embraced her, and rolled on the floor. The husband stood there in a panic. He had called him, what else could he do? When the locals learned of this, they arrived armed with wooden logs and palm fronds. Then this man slowly stood up and said, "It is done, it is all done," and simply walked away. The woman's stomach pain vanished. What do we understand from this? The dirt rolled from their sweat is termed 'Ramakkatti'. Only sanyasis know of it. This sweat, this dirt, this saliva—if all this rubs off from their body, it is considered a medicine. For this, one should remain unbathed. If he bathes, this will not be obtained. Isn't it washed away by daily bathing? Then only the fresh sweat will be available, right? If they remain unbathed with the sweat, just rolling this dirt from it and administering it is sufficient for the patient. This is called Ramakkatti. If you hear this, you might express disgust. Their sweat and dirt cure illnesses. Why is this mentioned? That is the conduct of an avadhuta. It is for those who serve as such messengers. Through ashram life, we must comprehend each of these concepts. This must also be imparted to society. For that, those residing in the ashram must understand these things prudently. There are many who travel upon the path of self-realization. If one lacks prudence, they might unknowingly insult such great souls. That will lead to profound destruction.
Guruvani
December 1985

In our midst, if we mention terms like Karma, Yoga, Sanyasa, or Jnana, it cannot be said that we possess significant knowledge about them. Perhaps it might be found in a few isolated individuals. This is primarily due to the historical shortcomings of our environment. Firstly—the state. We lack the familiarity to even examine the nature of statecraft that has existed in governance up to this day. Statecraft requires comprehensive knowledge on both a national and global scale. The governance system must guide and rectify what needs to happen in the world. We have not had the opportunity to acquire such knowledge. By 'we', I mean the Shudra class. The reason the Shudra class did not attain it was because, according to the laws of Manu, it was written that they had no right to rule. It is no longer possible to examine whether this was right or wrong. Therefore, if necessary, they had to be made Kshatriyas in order to rule. You must be aware of the political tales behind conferring Kshatriya status. Or haven't you seen the futile efforts made to elevate even Sree Chithira Thirunal to Kshatriya status? We know this without having to ask anyone. It is impossible for such knowledge to reach the Shudra class. The denial of literacy is the primary reason for this. In an illiterate community, we cannot expect to find this aforementioned statecraft—or authoritative religious texts like the Puranas, Upanishads, or Vedas. If we pass long periods without knowing any of this, won't we become incapable of knowing who the ruler of this nation is or how to function within the foundational systems of the world? Then, we would just eat whatever we get and celebrate whatever we see. We had no knowledge beyond that. Due to the grace of time, we are now in a position to attain this. There is a decree that what happened in the Treta and Dvapara Yugas should not happen in the Kali Yuga. For that purpose, the divine will had taken precautionary measures back then. Because we cannot understand this, it still seems like an insurmountable mountain to us. The reason for this inability to understand is what was mentioned above.
